about:
# Priestly Forever

**Priestly** is a lightweight buff manager for priests, inspired by **PallyPower**. It tracks
*Power Word: Fortitude*, *Divine Spirit* and *Shadow Protection* across your party or raid and lets
you rebuff with a single click.

This is the **World of Warcraft: Forever** edition (client 1.60.1, Interface `16001`).

> **[Buffy](https://github.com/Spotnick2/Buffy) is the new consolidated version.** It combines
> Priestly, Magely and Wildly in one addon on the same engine, and picks Priest, Mage or Druid
> buffs for the character you log in. It starts with fresh settings rather than importing
> Priestly's, so disable Priestly while you use it, or you get two buff windows.

![Priestly buff window in a group](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Spotnick2/priestly/main/docs/screenshots/priestly-05.gif)

*Example from an earlier build; the current window has additional controls.*

> **Playing TBC Classic Anniversary?** Install **v1.0.6** — the last release for that client. It
> stays available on CurseForge and the CurseForge app will keep offering it for the Anniversary
> game version. The Anniversary line is no longer being developed.

---

## Features

* **One row per group, per buff** — colour-coded by how many people are missing it, with the lowest
  remaining timer on the bar.
* **One-click buffing** — left-click casts the group Prayer, right-click buffs the first person
  missing it. No targeting.
* **Works before you have the Prayers** — while you only know the single-target spells, left-click
  simply buffs whoever needs it. Nothing is wired to a spell you do not have.
* **Per-member popover** — mouse over a row for the full list with range indicators and per-person
  click casting.
* **Group-aware** — follows party and raid changes, subgroups, and pets. Hunter and Warlock pets
  are never listed: on Forever they scale from their master.
* **Reagent tracking** — shows the candles and Light Feathers needed by spells you know.
* **Shadow Protection when it counts** — always, only when someone in the group already has it, or
  only inside instances you pick.
* **Window controls** — minimize without closing, lock its position, adjust opacity and choose
  which side the member popover opens on.

---

## Usage

```
/priestly          toggle the window
/priestly show     force open
/priestly hide     close
/priestly config   open the options panel
/priestly reset    reset the window position
/priestly pos      explain the window's saved position
/priestly adopt    use this character's old settings for all your priests
/priestly help     full command and click reference, then the spell names Priestly reads
```

If a member shows `?`, note where it appears: beside the class icon it means the
spell's range is unknown; in place of a timer it means the buff cannot be read and
there is no cached observation. These are independent, and neither proves a language
problem. For a battleground report, include a screenshot showing the column, whether
you are in combat, whether it recovers afterwards, and the spell-name report at the
end of `/priestly help` (locale, game build, addon/library versions and resolved names).

The window opens on its own when you join a group.

Settings persist between sessions. Buff choices and window options are shared across your priests;
whether the window is open is saved per character. If you previously configured different priests
and want one character's older setup to become the shared setup, log into that character and use
`/priestly adopt`.

Use **-** in the header to minimize to a small header, and **+** to restore the
buff rows. This keeps the window accessible; **X** still closes it. Minimize and
restore wait until combat ends. The choice lasts for the current session and
resets to expanded on `/reload` or login. Dragging, locking and resetting the
window work in either mode outside combat.

**Row colours:** green = everyone has it · yellow = some missing · red = nobody has it ·
grey `?` = buff state cannot be read right now (the client hides aura data during combat; Priestly
keeps counting down from the last reading instead of guessing).

---

## Installation

### CurseForge (recommended)

Install through the CurseForge app and enable it in game.

### GitHub and Wago

Download from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/Spotnick2/priestly/releases/latest)
or [Wago Addons](https://addons.wago.io/addons/priestly-priest-buff-manager-pally-power-style).
Both include the required libraries.

### Manual

Download the release zip and extract it so the folder lands at:

```
World of Warcraft/_forever_/Interface/AddOns/Priestly/
```

---

## Good to know

Priestly uses single-target buffs until you learn the corresponding Prayer. It learns buff
durations from live auras and relearns them when the client build changes. If an instance is
missing from the Shadow Protection list, please report its in-game name.

Forever can hide aura data during combat. When it does, Priestly uses its last observation and
shows `?` if no reliable reading is available. Window movement, closing and minimize/restore
requests made during combat take effect after combat ends.

A world buff such as Might of Stormwind or Warchief's Blessing, or Camp Benefits, can make the
game refuse Power Word: Fortitude with "A more powerful spell is already active". When that happens
out of combat to the rank the row casts, whether you cast it from the window, an action bar or a
macro, the row's single-target click moves on to the next member for up to 30 seconds, or until that
member's buffs change. You can still pick them from the popover. A refused lower rank, a refusal in
combat and one on a pet change nothing: the click aims as before.

The window's text uses the font for your game's language, so a Korean or Chinese client shows
names and labels as text. A Korean or Chinese character name on an English client still shows as
boxes: the client's English font has no such characters.

---

## Feedback

Open an [issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Spotnick2/priestly/issues) or leave a comment on
CurseForge. Include whether the problem happened in combat, a screenshot if the display looks
wrong, and the lines `/priestly help` ends with: your locale, game build, Priestly and library
versions, and the spell names Priestly reads from the client, with any it could not read flagged.
Use `/console scriptErrors 1` to show Lua errors that the client otherwise hides.

releases.name: Priestly Forever 2.1.3
releases.notes:
### Fixed
- Out of combat, when the game refuses a single-target buff on a group member with "A more
  powerful spell is already active" (a world buff such as Might of Stormwind or Warchief's
  Blessing, or Camp Benefits), the row's single-target click now moves on to the next member
  instead of trying the same one again: the left click, or the right click once you know Prayer
  of Fortitude (which is unchanged). The refused cast can come from the window, an action bar or a
  macro, as long as it is the rank the row casts. It tries that member again after 30 seconds, or
  sooner if their buffs change, and you can still pick them yourself from the popover. In combat,
  and on pets, the click aims as before. Needs LibGroupBuffs r39 (its refusal memory, LibGroupBuffs
  #97).

### Changed
- **Checked on game build 1.60.1.71091**, the current WoW: Forever client. Nothing Priestly relies on
  changed in this build, so there is nothing to do after updating.
- Updated the embedded LibGroupBuffs library from r36 to r39. Apart from the fix above, the
  window looks and behaves as before. LibGlass stays at r13. The fix was checked in game with
  Buffy, which runs on the same LibGroupBuffs r39.

releases.name: Priestly Forever 2.1.2
releases.notes:
### Fixed
- Hunter and Warlock pets no longer count as missing Divine Spirit or Shadow Protection, or
  appear as their click targets, as with Fortitude. On Forever these pets scale from their
  master. Other pet types are unchanged.
- The pet option is now **Track other pets**, and its description says which pets it covers:
  Priestly never lists Hunter and Warlock pets, and lists other pets in your group.

### Changed
- **Checked on game build 1.60.1.71037**, the current WoW: Forever client. Nothing Priestly relies on
  changed in this build, so there is nothing to do after updating.
- Same libraries as v2.1.1: LibGroupBuffs r36 and LibGlass r13. The pet change has passed offline
  tests; its in-game check follows this release.

releases.name: Priestly Forever 2.1.1
releases.notes:
### Changed
- **Checked on game build 1.60.1.70959**, the current WoW: Forever client. Nothing Priestly relies on
  changed in this build, so there is nothing to do after updating.
- The buff window's text now uses the font for your game's language: on a Korean or Chinese client,
  names and labels show as text instead of empty boxes. English and other Latin-alphabet clients,
  and Russian, keep the same font as before. A Korean or Chinese character name on an English
  client still shows as boxes; that is a limit of the game client.
- Updated the embedded libraries: LibGroupBuffs r34 to r36 and LibGlass r11 to r13, both included
  in the download.

releases.name: Priestly 2.1.0
releases.notes:
### Changed
- Updated the embedded LibGroupBuffs library to r34. LibGlass stays at r11. The window looks
  and behaves as before.
- The spell report at the end of `/priestly help` now also counts names it cannot vouch for
  either way (built by an older copy of the library another addon loaded), apart from names it
  could not read from the client.

releases.name: Priestly 2.0.17
releases.notes:
### Added
- Header controls to minimize the window and restore it without closing it.
  Requests made in combat apply when combat ends. Minimized state is session-only.

### Changed
- The buff window and popup now sit below normal UI panels, including bags.
- Updated the embedded LibGroupBuffs library to r31 for minimize/restore controls
  and lower window layering.
- Updated the embedded LibGlass material from r8 to r11.

### Fixed
- `/priestly help` now distinguishes unknown spell range (`?` beside the class icon)
  from unreadable buff state (`?` instead of a timer).
- Hunter and Warlock pets no longer count as missing Fortitude or appear as Fortitude
  click targets. Forever deliberately prevents these pets from receiving stat buffs.
  Tracking for other priest buffs and other pet types is unchanged.
